newsitem.title: UK: London gold ticks higher in PM, but sheds gains.
newsitem.headline: London gold ticks higher in PM, but sheds gains.

text.p: Gold continued exploring firmer territory on Tuesday afternoon, but turned back after encountering resistance, while silver remained virtually static.
Bullion fixed slightly easier at $380.85 an ounce, compared to $381.00 in the morning.
Prices began edging higher overnight after Monday's London close of $379.90/$380.40, in what one technical analyst dubbed a minor correction since last week's slide to 18-month lows.
"It's still in the $378-$382 range," which has contained prices for the past week, a dealer noted. Prices eased back after hitting a high bid of $381.90 not long before the fix.
Technically, gold needed to hurdle $381.70 which would then target the $384 area which would cap the rise, said technical analyst Karen Jones of Credit Suisse.
"The upside at this point is limited and I am still quite bearish," Jones said. "The break lower last week below $378.40 does not leave this market looking very healthy."
Silver continued ignoring gold's incremental march higher and was barely changed from Monday's London close. It was indicated at $4.90/$4.92, up just one cent.
"Silver is lagging behind gold on this," a dealer said. "There's a real lack of any sort of demand."

Some dealers and analysts said they were not convinced gold and silver had exhausted their downside potential. Investor demand remained weak while stock and bond markets boomed and physical offtake was low in anticipation of gold hitting bottom.
If they continued trending lower, gold was heading to $375 and then $370. Silver would target first $4.75 and then $4.65.
Still, short-term moving averages for both metals were starting to flattening out for the first time since they set off on a steep downward slope over a month ago.
That led some dealers to forecast that gold, at least, was starting to bottom out.
The platinum group metals diverged, with platinum pushing higher and palladium steadily losing ground.
"Platinum has been holding in there quite well. If it gets up to $385, we could see $390 soon enough," a dealer said.
Platinum was up $0.60 at $384.50/$385.50, after hitting a high bid of $385.50.

But palladium was indicated $1.25 lower at $117.75/$118.75. Dealers said it was in danger of further losses with slack demand from Japan's key electronics industry and soggy technical support below the important $120 level before $115.
